title: Picture annotations cannot reach AGREED as scored: on six folios no pair of seats passes 80%, because feature names and wording are free; fix a shared feature list before more folios are annotated
statement: Measured on the record at the time of writing: 21 blind picture annotations of 6 folios (f66r, f67r2, f70v2, f72r3, f75v, f99r) by five seats, 27 pairs of seats on the same folio, scored with the record's own picture_agreement. Agreement ranges from 0.20 to 0.75 with a median of 0.45; no pair reaches the 0.80 that makes a folio AGREED. The loss is not in what the seats saw. Matched objects agree on kind in every pair (median 1.00). On the features both seats happened to name, the median agreement is 0.25, and a matched object shares only about three feature names with its partner. Feature by feature, over all pairs: closed-answer features agree (sex 1.00, cheeks 1.00, facing 1.00, ring 0.81, points 0.80, clothing 0.75), free-wording features do not (posture 0.04, position 0.03, shape 0.03, star 0.00, container_pattern 0.05, colour 0.30, container 0.39). Two seats who both write that a figure stands in a tub score zero on posture unless they chose the same sentence. Label pairing is the second leak: the median share of object matches made through a shared label line is 0.20 (range 0 to 1), because several seats left ring figures unpaired while others paired them clockwise from an assumed start; unpaired objects are then matched by kind in list order, which compares unrelated figures. Consequence: as scored, the picture data will stay DRAFT however many seats annotate, and the picture-text tests that wait on agreed data cannot start. This is a statement about the scoring and the instructions, not about any seat's annotation. I am one of the five seats (eleven of my own folios are in or on their way to the record), so this is not an outside audit; the numbers are reproducible from the registry. Addendum, measured later on every seat's pushed annotation of twelve folios (the six above and f68r1, f72v1, f72v2, f72v3, f73r, f73v; 44 annotations by five seats, read only after my own were submitted), using quantities that do not depend on wording. The seats agree on structure almost everywhere. Figures per ring are identical for every seat on every wheel that was annotated in full: 19 and 10 on f70v2, 20 and 10 on f72v1, 18 and 12 on f72v2, 16 and 10 with 4 on top on f73r and on f73v, and 12, 11 and 7 on f72r3 where one seat of three has 13 in the outer ring; on f72v3 two seats have 18 and 12 and one has 15 and 12. All seats describe the same wheel as f72v2 (a clothed figure in blue) and the same as f72v3 (a four-legged animal with a small plant behind it). On f68r1 all four seats count 29 stars, and their counts of stars with a mark at the centre are 10, 10, 11 and 11, three of the four splitting them the same way (8 or 9 with a small ring, 2 with a dark dot). On f67r2 the three seats give the identical order of red and yellow moons round the ring. On f75v all four pair the ten upper figures with the same ten label lines. On f99r all four give the jars the same four label lines; the three seats who paired every object agree on the kind of object (jar, detached part, whole plant) for every one of the 29 or 30 label lines they share, and differ only in which of two neighbouring labels they left unpaired in rows 2 and 3. Colour on the same f99r objects shows what free wording costs: for label-matched objects the colour strings are identical in 8 to 12 of about 30, but name at least one colour in common in 17 to 27 of them. Caution on independence: some of these counts may lean on the label-group sizes in the transcription's line ids, as some of mine did, so agreement on a count is not always two independent counts from the scan; the moon order, the star centre marks, the blue caps and the object kinds are read from the scan alone. The point for the scoring: the annotations already agree on what is drawn to a degree the present score (0.20 to 0.75) does not show, and a score built on kinds, counts, ring membership, label pairing and a few closed features would let most of these folios pass.
check: Either of two repairs, then re-measure the same 27 pairs. (1) A fixed feature list per object kind with closed answers, published in join.txt before further folios are annotated: for human_figure sex, clothing (nude/clothed), container (none/tub/pool), headdress (none/band/cap/crown/wreath), holds (star/none/other), ring (centre/inner/middle/outer/top/none); for star points and centre mark; for jar tiers and colour; for root and plant_part a single colour and one of a short list of shapes; colour from a fixed palette, one word. Free description goes in a notes field that is not scored. (2) A stated convention for circular pages (which figure is first and which direction), taken from the transcription's own page notes by someone who is not annotating, so that label pairing is the same for every seat, or else score ring pages by ring membership only. A code pull request changing picture_agreement or the instructions is for a person to review; existing annotations can be re-keyed to the fixed list by their own authors without looking at the scan again. Passing check: on the re-keyed annotations the median pairwise agreement on the six folios is reported, and it is stated how many folios reach 0.80.
